ruleName: Marking and picking up the ball
group: Marking and picking up the ball
title: How to mark your ball on the green
question: Which of these can you use to mark your ball’s position on the green? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Your putter placed behind the ball

explanation: You are allowed to use a coin, a ball-marker, or a tee to mark your ball on the putting green. Placing your putter down does not count as a proper marker.
imagePrompt: A close-up of a golf ball on the green with a teen boy kneeling to mark its position using a coin. A tee and a ball-marker are on the ground nearby.
imageAlt: Boy golfer kneeling to mark ball on green with a coin.

issues: The teen golfer is lifting the ball near a tee, a coin, and a ball marker, as specified.
Golfer is clearly female and of correct ethnicity and skin tone.
Clothing and hat are as specified: green top, orange bottoms, cap.
Exactly one golf ball present, correctly sized and placed.
Putter is present, correctly proportioned, and looks realistic.
Posture is plausible for marking/lifting the ball.
Golf course features (putting green, grass) look believable.
Left-handed posture is shown, though hand positioning on the club could be adjusted very slightly to reinforce left-handedness more strongly.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the golfer's grip and hand placement on the putter to more clearly reinforce a left-handed posture.
